requirements.note: The release announcement gives 2 GB RAM and 20 GB of disk as the minimums, and recommends 4 GB RAM and 100 GB of disk for a comfortable install.

page.description: Linux Mint editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: The Ubuntu-based desktop with its own Cinnamon shell and a conservative update policy. Pick an edition, then write the 64-bit image to a USB stick.
pros: Cinnamon, MATE and Xfce editions, all on the same Ubuntu 24.04 base.
Updates arrive slowly on purpose: Mint's own Update Manager decides what is offered.
Written for people coming from Windows, with the desktop laid out as expected.
cons: 64-bit only: there is no 32-bit image for very old machines.
The regular ISOs carry kernel 6.14; very new AMD hardware may need an HWE image instead.
Based on Ubuntu 24.04, so it trails the current Ubuntu LTS.
Snap is disabled by default, so instructions written for Ubuntu snap packages need extra steps.

page.status: One official path per edition: the 64-bit ISO, written with Mint's USB Image Writer, GNOME Disks or dd. Writing erases the stick; the installer's erase-disk option erases the target disk.
